feedback: Evidence base: iteration 1 (kp 2.5, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.6, sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02, sensor_size 0.008) scored 55.46. All 60 trials went off track. Progress was 0.11 to 0.16, max_error was 0.061 to 0.063 m (just over the 0.06 m limit), and s-bend and slalom each had about 2 line-loss events. Iteration 0 (kp 4.0, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.8) had the same geometry and also failed on every trial, so gain changes alone have not fixed the failure. Read from the candidate itself: the sensors span only +/-0.02 m, while the tape edge sits at 0.0125 m, so the outer sensors lose the tape at roughly 0.02 m of drift. The wider array (x = -0.04 to +0.04), the larger sensor_size (0.012 m) and kp 3.5 address that directly. All values are inside the public contract. The main uncertainty is that the signal scale changes with spacing, so kp 3.5 may over- or under-steer. I have no measured outcome for this candidate, so the next race decides the next step. If line_loss_events fall to 0 or 1 and max_error stays under 0.06 m, keep the geometry and move base_speed toward 2.0 for completion time. If runs still leave the track with about 2 line-loss events, test line_loss 'search_left' or 'search_right' with this geometry before more gain changes. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15, lower kp toward 2.5.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events fall to 0 or 1 and max_error stays below 0.06 m but runs do not finish: raise controller.base_speed from 1.6 toward 2.0, keeping kp 3.5, kd 0.3 and the wider geometry, since the line is now held.

If runs still leave the track with line_loss_events near 2: keep the geometry and change controller.line_loss from 'last_direction' to 'search_left' or 'search_right', since iteration 1 showed gains alone did not stop the loss at the 0.06 m limit.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 with the robot staying on track: lower controller.kp from 3.5 toward 2.5 to match the wider sensor signal, keeping kd at 0.3 and the sensor geometry unchanged.
